messages.subject: SECR on polygons area search
parts:
Hello! I am quite new to R and the secr package, so I am probably asking dull questions; I swear by the way that I post this afer a long period of trial, not wanting to abuse of anyone!
I am studying a fox population in the Alps; on an area of interest I plotted 8 detatched zones wich I searched uniformely looking for scat to be genotyped. Meanwhile, having the spatial points of the samples, I run a simulation with a made up capture history (I jointed the trap file "Buffer2Vertici.txt" and the capure file "captXY.txt" with make.capthist, then run secr.fit) and obtained an output that I just don't understand: why are the estimates of Density and Sigma so low? During the R run most of the simulation held a negative outcome fore those parameters: how is that possible? Also, I made another run changing the coarseness of the mask points, but outputs were exactely the same. Shouldn't that change something?

I hope to ameliorate the fitness of the model to the sampling design as I go on; meanwhile I thank you all for the useful package AND the forum, and I wish you good work!

Roberto

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: SECR on polygons area search
parts:
Hi Roberto

Your results don't look so bad to me. Density is always animals per hectare - multiply by 100 for animals / km^2 (0.5 foxes/km^2?). The interim values shown during likelihood maximisation (trace = TRUE) are on the link scale (i.e. log of D, log of sigma).

I think you need a much larger buffer (>=6000 not 700 m, given sigma 1500-2000 m). Maybe also you can clip parts of the mask as 'non-habitat'. And at present you don't actually use zonemask; replace buffer = 700 with mask = zonemask in your call to secr.fit.

I note that secr.fit is painfully slow with your data (my test has barely begun) - I guess that's because you searched several fairly complex polygons. It is appropriate to use the 'polygon' detector type because foxes may be detected in more than one polygon per occasion, but for experimentation you might find it expedient (faster) to use the polygonX detector type.

Murray

parts:
Hello and thank you for the really quick support!

I definetively overreact to the output values; i thaught that Density was ind/km^2 and had no idea of the log scale of likelyhood maximization! And yep, not using "zonemask" was dumb, too! Thanx.

I followed your suggestion to enlarge the buffer, but that gave me warnings I did not get before:

Warning messages:
1: In secr.fit(CAPTHIST, model = D ~ 1, mask = zonemask, trace = TRUE,  :
  using default starting values
2: In secr.fit(CAPTHIST, model = D ~ 1, mask = zonemask, trace = TRUE,  :
  possible maximization error: nlm returned code 3. See ?nlm
3: In secr.fit(CAPTHIST, model = D ~ 1, mask = zonemask, trace = TRUE,  :
  at least one variance calculation failed

It resulted in NaNs, as visible in "outp.txt"...what's that?!

I think one can assume that there is no non-habitat area in the location I sampled (basically because foxes just don't care), but I am thinking to set different detection probabilities at local level, I suppose in a "rasterization" fashion! Is that possible (thou note 2 in "Polygon and transect detectors in secr 3.1" worries me)?

I am trying the polygonX as you suggested; thank you again and good evening!

Roberto

It worked for me (slightly different settings, and buffer probably still to narrow)
library(secr)
setwd('c:/density users/Robert Celva')
vertici <- read.traps ('buffer2vertici.txt', detector = 'polygon')
capt <- read.table ('captXY.txt')
ch <- make.capthist (capt, vertici, fmt = 'XY')
msk <- make.mask(vertici, buffer = 6000, type = 'trapbuffer')
fit <- secr.fit(ch, mask = msk)
fit

messages.subject: Re: SECR on polygons area search
parts:
It would help to know how you used polygonX and how R "crashed".

It is no problem to fit a patch-level covariate where patch = searched polygon. Just assign covariates(vertici) <- data.frame(soil = c(1,2,1,1,2,1,1,2)) or whatever your soil types are, one per polygon. Then use e.g. g0~soil in your model. There is no mechanism for modelling within-patch variation.

Murray

On Saturday, 1 September 2018 13:03:37 UTC+2, Murray Efford wrote:

It would help to know how you used polygonX and how R "crashed".

It is no problem to fit a patch-level covariate where patch = searched polygon. Just assign covariates(vertici) <- data.frame(soil = c(1,2,1,1,2,1,1,2)) or whatever your soil types are, one per polygon. Then use e.g. g0~soil in your model. There is no mechanism for modelling within-patch variation.

Murray

On Monday, 27 August 2018 18:15:57 UTC+2, Murray Efford wrote:
Hi Roberto

Your results don't look so bad to me. Density is always animals per hectare - multiply by 100 for animals / km^2 (0.5 foxes/km^2?). The interim values shown during likelihood maximisation (trace = TRUE) are on the link scale (i.e. log of D, log of sigma).

I think you need a much larger buffer (>=6000 not 700 m, given sigma 1500-2000 m). Maybe also you can clip parts of the mask as 'non-habitat'. And at present you don't actually use zonemask; replace buffer = 700 with mask = zonemask in your call to secr.fit.

I note that secr.fit is painfully slow with your data (my test has barely begun) - I guess that's because you searched several fairly complex polygons. It is appropriate to use the 'polygon' detector type because foxes may be detected in more than one polygon per occasion, but for experimentation you might find it expedient (faster) to use the polygonX detector type.

Murray
